ambient_events: A sheet of something lets go high up the stack, slides, and stops.
The crane cable creaks, swings a hand-width, and settles.
Water finds a path through three cars and arrives at your collar.
Somewhere in the rows a spring lets go with a noise like a small animal.
The wind comes through the aisles and plays the whole yard like a bad flute.
description: Bales of crushed car in rows two and three high, stacked with the crane's rough sense of level and gone the deep orange-brown of old iron that has stopped pretending. Between them: aisles wide enough for one person and a wheelbarrow. Everything drips. The ground is a compacted crust of glass, rust flake and forty years of dropped bolts, and it crunches with every step in a way that means you are never anywhere quietly. Overhead the grabber crane hangs open on its cable, jaws apart, waiting. Back east to the shack.
name: The Rows
